If I tried to move my hand forward while on a ship traveling at the speed of light, what would happen?
I believe you would move relative to your surroundings. To you it wouldn't feel like you're moving at light speed.

While you are moving at the speed of light, you won't feel like you are travelling at the speed of light (think travelling on a fast moving train. without windows or any sort of bumps, you won't be able to tell you are moving at all). So while you walk around on that ship travelling at near the speed of light, all you can tell is that you are moving at a walking pace.

However, to someone outside of the ship who is not travelling at the speed of light, it begins to get a bit crazy. This is where my understanding gets a bit fuzzy. I believe to the outside observer, the person on the ship gains additional mass, and the person's observed velocity might increase fractionally, but will never reach the speed of light.

disclaimer: Took half a semester of special relativity and it has been several years since school.

I would default to your answer because I have not taken any classes on such a thing, but intuitively it seems like an outside observer would not see any movement. All they would see is first here, then there with no intermediate movement. I'm assuming that's wrong though, because little do things adhere to intuition when traveling at the speed of light.

There's no way to answer this, because, so far as we know, you can't travel at the speed of light. You can get really, really, close, hypothetically, but you can't reach the speed of light.

So the real answer to this is...nobody knows.
